TITLE: Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 in Germany: International Postdoctoral Researchers Can Receive €3,000 Per Month for Contemporary History Research

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
International historians and postdoctoral researchers specializing in twentieth-century German, European, or Eastern European history have an opportunity to spend two months conducting independent research in Germany through the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam (Leibniz-Zentrum für Zeithistorische Forschung Potsdam – ZZF).

For the 2027 fellowship cycle, ZZF is inviting applications for two Leibniz Summer Fellowships focused on German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century. The program is specifically intended for international scholars who already hold a doctoral degree and are residing outside Germany when they apply.

Successful fellows will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam between April and October 2027. Each fellow will receive a monthly grant of €3,000, meaning that a two-month fellowship provides €6,000 in total grant support. The funding is intended to cover the fellow’s living costs, travel and appropriate insurance during the fellowship period.

The application deadline is November 30, 2026.

About the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027

The Leibniz Summer Fellowship is a research residency offered by the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam for established international scholars working in areas relevant to twentieth-century German and European history.

The program combines two important elements: independent scholarly research and active participation in the intellectual life of ZZF.

Rather than requiring fellows to work on a predetermined institutional project, ZZF allows successful applicants to continue research based on their own scholarly interests. Preference, however, is given to proposals that connect with one or more of the Centre’s existing research departments.

This approach makes the fellowship particularly attractive to postdoctoral historians who already have a developed research agenda and would benefit from access to German academic networks, historical resources and interaction with specialists working on related themes.

Host Institution: Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam

The Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam, commonly known as ZZF, is a major German research institute specializing in twentieth-century contemporary history and its connections with the present.

Its work places particular emphasis on German and European social history after 1945 while situating those developments within broader international contexts. In addition to fundamental historical research, ZZF is involved in research infrastructure, digital knowledge transfer and cooperation with universities and research institutions in Germany and abroad.

ZZF is a member of the Leibniz Association, one of Germany’s major networks of non-university research institutions. The Centre has held Leibniz Association membership since 2009 and receives institutional support from both federal and state-level public funding.

The institute also has an extensive international academic orientation, including cooperation with universities and research organizations as well as a visiting-researcher program. These connections help make the fellowship more than simply a short period of individual archival or library research.

Two Fellowships Available for 2027

ZZF has announced two positions under the 2027 Leibniz Summer Fellowship program.

The thematic field is:

German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century

This is broad enough to accommodate scholars working across multiple subfields of contemporary history, provided that their research has a substantive connection to German or European twentieth-century history.

The opportunity is intended for international postdoctoral researchers rather than doctoral students or applicants who have not yet completed their doctorate.

Fellowship Duration

Each fellowship lasts for:

Two consecutive months

The research stay must take place between:

April and October 2027

Successful candidates are expected to live in either Berlin or Potsdam, Germany, throughout their two-month fellowship period.

Applicants should therefore consider their availability carefully before applying and identify a feasible two-month period within the April-to-October window.

The requirement to remain locally based is important because the program is designed around participation in ZZF’s academic environment rather than functioning as a remote research grant.

Financial Support: €3,000 Per Month

One of the major features of the Leibniz Summer Fellowship is its financial support.

Each successful fellow receives:

€3,000 per month

Because the fellowship runs for two months, the total fellowship grant amounts to:

€6,000 for the full two-month period

ZZF states that this funding is expected to cover costs associated with the fellowship, including:

Living expenses

Travel expenses

Appropriate insurance

Applicants should understand that these costs are expected to be met from the €3,000 monthly fellowship payment rather than assuming that accommodation, flights or insurance will automatically be paid separately by the institution.

Researchers considering the fellowship should therefore prepare an estimated budget covering transportation to Germany, temporary accommodation in Berlin or Potsdam, local transportation, meals, insurance and other personal expenses.

Research Facilities Provided by ZZF

In addition to the financial grant, fellows receive access to institutional research infrastructure.

ZZF states that fellowship recipients will be provided with facilities including:

Office space

Computer access

Other relevant institutional facilities

These resources are designed to allow fellows to work from the Centre and participate meaningfully in its research community.

This is particularly valuable for international researchers who want more than financial support and instead seek an immersive period within a specialist academic environment.

Access to an Important Contemporary History Library

Research fellows can also benefit from ZZF’s specialist library.

The ZZF library concentrates on German and European contemporary history after 1945 and includes material covering social and economic history, political and cultural history, media history, and the history of German division and reunification.

Its catalogue also incorporates electronic and audiovisual resources, journal holdings and thousands of indexed academic articles.

For scholars whose work relies on German-language scholarship or European contemporary history literature, proximity to such a specialized research collection can considerably strengthen a short research stay.

ZZF’s Main Research Departments

Applicants have considerable freedom to pursue their own research, but there is a strategic advantage in demonstrating how a proposed project connects with ZZF’s institutional expertise.

The Centre’s academic research is structured around five major research areas:

Communism and Society

Knowledge – Economy – Politics

Media and Information Society

Regimes of the Social Sphere

Globalizations in a Divided World

ZZF’s overall research agenda covers twentieth-century German and European contemporary history from political, social, cultural, economic, media and transnational perspectives.

Applicants should therefore study these departments before preparing their project proposal and identify where their own work has an intellectual connection with ZZF researchers.

Research on Communism, Eastern Europe and Post-Communist Transformation

Scholars specializing in Eastern European history may find the fellowship particularly relevant.

For example, ZZF’s Communism and Society department examines governance and social practices in the German Democratic Republic and Central and Eastern Europe. Its research also addresses transformations surrounding and extending beyond the political changes of 1989–1991, along with issues including violence, civil society and social developments in late and post-communist societies.

This institutional expertise helps explain why the fellowship announcement explicitly includes Eastern European history within its thematic scope.

Global and Transnational Perspectives

The Centre’s work is not limited to national German history.

Its research also examines how German and European societies interacted with wider global transformations, including the Cold War, decolonization, changing international orders and transnational connections.

ZZF’s work on globalization examines how European societies both influenced and were influenced by international structures and cross-border developments.

Applicants whose projects use comparative, transnational or global-history approaches may therefore find relevant intellectual connections at the Centre.

Who Is Eligible for the Leibniz Summer Fellowships?

Eligibility is comparatively straightforward but academically demanding.

Applicants must meet the following central conditions:

Hold a doctoral degree at the time the application is submitted

Have postdoctoral standing

Demonstrate an outstanding academic record

Be an international applicant

Reside outside Germany at the time of application

Propose research relevant to twentieth-century German and/or European history, including Eastern European history

ZZF explicitly defines the international character of the fellowship in terms of residence: applicants should be based outside Germany.

This is therefore not a fellowship for applicants who are still completing their PhD or expect to receive the doctorate only after submitting the application.

Do You Need to Be a German Citizen?

No nationality requirement restricting the fellowship to German citizens is stated.

In fact, the fellowship is designed for international researchers residing outside Germany.

This means applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe outside Germany, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may potentially apply, provided they meet the academic and residency requirements and their proposed research fits the fellowship’s scholarly field.

Nationality and residence should not, however, be confused. The explicit requirement concerns being an international applicant residing outside Germany at application stage.

What Academic Background Is Required?

This is an advanced research fellowship rather than a student scholarship.

A completed doctoral degree is mandatory.

The official call additionally emphasizes postdoctoral standing and a strong academic record.

Accordingly, the fellowship is most appropriate for researchers such as:

Postdoctoral scholars

University lecturers

Academic historians

Research fellows

Early- or mid-career researchers with completed PhDs

Independent scholars with an established academic record, provided they satisfy the formal requirements

The strongest applicants are likely to have a clearly defined research agenda, publications or other evidence of scholarly achievement and a project that can make productive use of a two-month stay at ZZF.

Research Project Requirements

Applicants are not required to join a predetermined research project.

Instead, fellows can pursue their own individual research interests.

However, ZZF specifically indicates that preference will be given to applicants whose projects relate to one or more of its research departments.

Applicants should therefore avoid presenting the proposed project as completely isolated from the host institution.

A strong proposal should explain why conducting the research specifically at ZZF would be useful.

Relevant questions to address when developing the proposal include:

How does the project relate to contemporary German or European history?

Does it engage with Eastern European history where relevant?

Which ZZF department has the strongest connection with the project?

Which methodological or thematic conversations at ZZF could benefit the research?

What specific progress can realistically be achieved within two months?

Why is residence in Berlin or Potsdam valuable for the project?

What scholarly output may result from the fellowship?

These are strategic application considerations rather than additional formal requirements published by ZZF.

Integration Into ZZF’s Academic Community

Successful applicants will not simply receive funding and work independently.

Each fellow will be affiliated with one of ZZF’s research departments.

Fellows will be able to participate in departmental academic activities and will also be expected to present their research project through the institute’s research seminar.

This makes communication skills and willingness to engage academically with other researchers important aspects of the fellowship experience.

Applicants should therefore approach the program as both an individual research residency and an academic-exchange opportunity.

Required Application Documents

The application package consists of four main documents:

Letter of Interest

Curriculum Vitae

List of Publications

Research Project Proposal of no more than 1,500 words

All documents must be combined into one PDF attachment and submitted electronically.

The application may be prepared in either:

English or German

This allows international scholars who do not write academically in German to apply in English.

No Recommendation Letter Required

An important feature of the application process is that applicants do not need to submit a letter of recommendation.

This simplifies the application process because candidates do not have to arrange an external academic referee or wait for recommendation letters before the deadline.

The application will therefore depend heavily on the quality of the applicant’s own academic record, CV, publication record, statement of interest and research proposal.

How to Prepare the 1,500-Word Project Proposal

The project proposal is likely to be one of the most important components of the application.

Because it cannot exceed 1,500 words, applicants should make every section purposeful.

A useful structure could include:

Research Title

Use a precise academic title reflecting the central historical question or argument.

Research Background

Briefly explain the historical issue, scholarly debate or research gap that motivates the project.

Research Questions

State clearly what the project seeks to investigate.

Sources and Methodology

Identify the types of sources, archives, publications or methodological approaches that will be used.

Contribution to Scholarship

Explain what new knowledge, argument or perspective the project could add to existing research.

Relevance to ZZF

Identify the ZZF department or research themes that connect most directly with the project.

Fellowship Work Plan

Explain what can realistically be accomplished during the two-month stay.

This suggested structure is application guidance rather than a format mandated by the official call.

How to Prepare the Letter of Interest

The letter of interest should complement rather than duplicate the research proposal.

Applicants can use it to explain:

Their current academic position and research trajectory

Why they are applying for the Leibniz Summer Fellowship

Why ZZF is an appropriate host institution

What they hope to achieve during the residency

How interaction with the Centre’s scholars may support the project

How the fellowship fits into their broader academic development

Candidates should keep the letter focused and professional.

Preparing the Publication List

Because ZZF asks applicants to demonstrate a strong academic record, the publication list provides important evidence of scholarly development.

Depending on the applicant’s career stage, it may include:

Peer-reviewed journal articles

Academic books or monographs

Edited volumes

Book chapters

Published research reports

Relevant scholarly publications

Applicants should provide complete bibliographical information and organize their publications clearly.

How to Submit the Application

Applications must be submitted electronically by email.

The official fellowship email address is:

fellowships@zzf-potsdam.de

All required documents should be consolidated into one PDF attachment. ZZF does not request a recommendation letter.

Applicants should carefully check that all four required components are included before sending the application.

Application Deadline

The final deadline is:

November 30, 2026

Applications should be completed and submitted by this date.

ZZF states that fellowship decisions will be communicated no later than:

December 31, 2026.

This relatively short decision period gives successful applicants several months to organize travel, accommodation, insurance and research arrangements before the fellowship period begins in April 2027.

Key Dates at a Glance

Stage
Date / Period

Application deadline
November 30, 2026

Fellowship decisions
By December 31, 2026

Fellowship period
Two consecutive months

Eligible residency window
April–October 2027

Location
Berlin or Potsdam, Germany

Monthly fellowship grant
€3,000

Total for two months
€6,000

These dates and funding conditions are stated in the official 2027 fellowship announcement.

Why Researchers Should Consider This Opportunity

For eligible historians, the Leibniz Summer Fellowship offers several advantages in one program.

It provides direct financial support, a temporary institutional base in Germany, access to academic facilities and the opportunity to interact with scholars specializing in contemporary European history.

The fellowship may be particularly useful for researchers who are:

Developing an article or book project on twentieth-century Europe

Conducting postdoctoral research involving Germany

Working on Central or Eastern European contemporary history

Expanding a project into comparative or transnational European history

Seeking intellectual exchange with German-based scholars

Planning research that benefits from spending time in Berlin or Potsdam

ZZF’s international cooperation, specialist research departments and contemporary-history resources provide an academic environment particularly relevant to these objectives.

Important Points to Remember Before Applying

Applicants should pay particular attention to several requirements.

First, a doctorate must already have been completed when the application is submitted.

Second, this call is intended for international applicants residing outside Germany.

Third, although applicants can propose their own research, aligning the proposal with ZZF’s research profile can strengthen its institutional relevance.

Fourth, the fellowship lasts exactly two consecutive months and fellows must reside in Berlin or Potsdam during that period.

Finally, the €3,000 monthly payment is intended to cover multiple types of expenditure, including living, travel and insurance costs. Applicants should therefore plan their budget accordingly.

Conclusion

The Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam offer an excellent short-term research opportunity for international postdoctoral historians interested in twentieth-century German, European or Eastern European history.

With two fellowships available, a €3,000 monthly grant, access to ZZF’s academic facilities and specialist research environment, and the opportunity to participate directly in departmental and seminar activities, the program provides both financial support and meaningful scholarly engagement.

Applicants must already hold a doctorate, demonstrate a strong academic record and reside outside Germany when applying. Successful researchers will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam sometime between April and October 2027.

The most important date to remember is November 30, 2026, when applications close. Candidates should prepare a letter of interest, CV, publication list and a research proposal of no more than 1,500 words, combine everything into one PDF and submit it to the official fellowship email address.

TITLE: 2022-23 Mellon/SAR Academic Freedom Workshop & Fellowships

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Protecting scholars and the freedom to think, question, and share ideas

Scholars at Risk (SAR) announces a call for applications for five remote research fellowships for early career researchers who investigate issues focusing upon academic freedom and/or related higher education values. The fellowship program, made possible by the generous support of and partnership with the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation, is intended to provide support for a professional community of researchers who wish to develop and share related work leading to the completion of a formal written publication, a new course offering, workshop, webinar or other significant end product.

Over the course of the eight-month program, from November 2022 to June 2023, fellows will complete their proposed project and participate in monthly remote, online workshop sessions during which they will be asked to present the progress of their work and to offer feedback on the work of other fellows. During the latter part of the program, fellows will be expected to prepare and deliver an online talk or presentation of their work for SAR staff, network members, and/or guests (with appropriate security accommodations, as necessary). Fellows are also expected to attend a virtual reunion meeting in September 2023 as SAR seeks to develop a community of academic freedom researchers. Fellows will receive a stipend of USD $8000 intended to cover research expenses, publication, or other costs, as the fellow may decide. In addition, participants will have the opportunity to gain exposure to SAR’s programming and to network with SAR partner-experts on academic freedom issues.

The deadline for submission is August 25, 2022, with decisions to be announced in October.

Criteria:

PhD degree received less than 8 years ago; in limited cases, doctoral candidates in the final stages of dissertation completion may be considered.

Current research or teaching affiliation with a higher education institution, association, or research organization.

Demonstrated interest in teaching, researching, or publishing about issues of academic freedom or related higher education values.

Preference for projects involving comparative, international, or collaborative work

(fellowship awards may be split across two researchers).

Commitment to participate in 8-10 remote, online workshops and/or public webinars with co-recipients, SAR staff, network members, and guests (with proper security accommodations).

Ability to lawfully receive stipend funds and complete program requirements in the

country of current location, assuming responsibility for tax or reporting requirements, if any.

Personal experiences with risk or threat are not a consideration for selection, but current or formerly at-risk researchers are encouraged to apply.

Candidates in or from the Global South and from minority or otherwise marginalized communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

Application Instructions

Applications may be submitted here through August 25, 2022. Applicants are required to submit an abstract, research plan and timeline, and a CV with the names and contact information of two references, in a single PDF, adhering to the criteria below. Applicants must also address questions regarding their proposed project through short-answer forms in the online application.

In a single PDF file, saved as “LAST NAME – Project Title”, please submit:

A 500-1000 word abstract* summarizing the formal research component of your

submission (guidelines below).

A research plan and timeline for the eighth month program (November 2022 – June 2023).

A CV and the contact information of two professional references who can speak to your candidacy for this fellowship program. If you have yet to complete your final degree, please include your expected date of completion.

Applications that do not include all the above will be ineligible for consideration.

Abstract Guidelines

What specific research question do you wish to address? What is its potential

significance?

How is your research question related to what is understood to entail academic

freedom and related values?

What methodology will you employ to address your research questions, and what types of evidence do you propose to gather?

How will your findings contribute to our greater understanding of what academic

freedom involves and how it can best be protected?

How does your proposed project fit within your current and long-term teaching,

research, and advocacy goals?

*The abstract refers to the formal publishable research proposed by the applicant, whereas the end product refers to both the research and the form(s) of its dissemination.

Short Answer Form

For the proposed end product of your project, please answer the following questions.

What objectives do you intend to achieve through completion of this end product?

In what form will your end product be delivered (webinar, podcast, journal article,

conference presentation, published curricular materials, etc.)?

What is your plan for disseminating the end product of your project?

Describe your target audience.

How will you assess the success of this portion of your project?

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – Firm Selection

Recent PhD graduates / post-docs and PhD students whose speciality is broadly in computer science, engineering, STEM and related areas.

Discuss and establish local priorities in the field of computational and artificial intelligence.

IEEE CIS International Mentoring Program

IEEE CIS Paper Development Workshop

Jointly co-design a plan for a range of engagement activities to be organised at future events.

A list of identified local stakeholders who are interested in attending and/or contributing to future engagement activities, including through hosting such events.

TITLE: 2027 NASA Hubble Fellowship Program (NHFP): Postdoctoral Fellowship in Astrophysics for International Scientists

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The 2027 NASA Hubble Fellowship Program (NHFP) is inviting applications from qualified postdoctoral scientists interested in conducting independent research that contributes to the field of NASA Astrophysics.

Administered by the Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI) on behalf of the NASA Astrophysics Division, the program supports researchers working in astronomy, physics, and related disciplines. Successful applicants will join one of three fellowship tracks — Einstein, Hubble, or Sagan Fellow — depending on their area of research.

The fellowship provides an opportunity for early-career scientists to pursue independent theoretical, observational, and/or instrumental research at a U.S. host institution of their choice, subject to the program’s host-institution rules.

Applications for the 2027 fellowship cycle opened on September 8, 2026, with applications due on October 28, 2026.

About the NASA Hubble Fellowship Program

The NASA Hubble Fellowship Program is a postdoctoral research fellowship program administered for NASA by the Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI).

The program is designed to support postdoctoral scientists conducting independent research that contributes to NASA’s astrophysics mission.

Research supported through the program can be:

Theoretical

Observational

Instrumental

Or a combination of these approaches

The program gives early-career scientists an opportunity to develop an independent research program while working at a U.S. host institution.

Depending on the research area, successful fellows will be designated as:

NASA Einstein Fellows

NASA Hubble Fellows

NASA Sagan Fellows

These fellowship designations correspond to different areas of astrophysical research within the broader NHFP program.

Who Can Apply for the 2027 NHFP?

The NASA Hubble Fellowship Program is open to applicants from all nationalities.

To be eligible, applicants must have completed or be expected to complete all requirements for their doctoral degree on or after January 1, 2023.

The doctorate must be in:

Astronomy

Physics

Or a related discipline

The program is therefore specifically designed for researchers at the postdoctoral stage who have recently completed, or are about to complete, their doctoral training.

Research Areas

NHFP fellows are expected to conduct independent research that contributes to NASA Astrophysics.

The program allows research to be theoretical, observational, instrumental, or a combination of these approaches.

This broad research structure means that applicants working across different areas of astrophysics may be able to develop fellowship proposals aligned with their specific scientific interests and expertise.

The fellowship designation awarded to a successful applicant — Einstein, Hubble, or Sagan — will depend on the applicant’s research area.

Fellowship Duration

The NASA Hubble Fellowship can last for up to three years.

The fellowship is structured as:

Initial one-year appointment

First annual renewal

Second annual renewal

The two renewals are contingent on:

Satisfactory performance

Availability of NASA funding

Therefore, although the program offers the possibility of a three-year fellowship, continuation beyond the initial appointment is not described as unconditional.

U.S. Host Institution

NHFP Fellowships are tenable at a U.S. host institution of the fellow’s choice.

However, the program places limits on the number of new fellows that can be hosted by an individual institution.

The stated policy allows:

A maximum of two new fellows per host institution per year

One new fellow for institutions that hosted two new fellows during the previous year

Host institutions must also have verified compliance with the NHFP employment policy.

Applicants should therefore review the official list of verified host institutions before finalizing their host-institution plans.

Number of Fellowships Available

For the 2027 cycle, the program anticipates offering up to 24 NHFP Fellowships.

The actual number of fellowships offered can therefore be up to 24 for the cycle.

Because this is a competitive postdoctoral research program, applicants should carefully follow the official application instructions and prepare their materials according to the requirements in the Announcement of Opportunity.

Organizations Administering the NHFP

The program is administered for NASA by the Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI).

STScI administers the program in collaboration with:

The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)

NASA Exoplanet Science Institute (NExScI) at the California Institute of Technology

The Chandra X-ray Center at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory

This collaborative structure connects the fellowship with several major institutions involved in astrophysical research.

What Fellows Will Do

The central purpose of the NHFP is to support postdoctoral scientists conducting independent research.

Research may involve theoretical investigations, observations, instrumentation, or combinations of these approaches.

The independent nature of the fellowship is particularly important because it allows postdoctoral researchers to develop their own research programs and contribute to the broader scientific objectives of NASA Astrophysics.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed research clearly demonstrates its relevance to astrophysics and its contribution to the scientific objectives of the program.

Applicants should pay close attention to two different deadlines: the main application deadline and the reference-letter deadline.

Applicants should carefully follow the instructions provided in the official NHFP Announcement of Opportunity.

Applicants should communicate with their chosen referees early enough to allow them to prepare and upload their letters before the separate reference-letter deadline.

The reference-letter deadline is:

The announcement specifically notes that referees will not receive an automated email containing an upload link.

Frequently Asked Questions

The NHFP encourages applicants to examine the program’s Frequently Asked Questions before submitting an application.

This can help applicants understand program policies and clarify requirements that may not be obvious from the basic fellowship announcement.

Because the fellowship has specific policies concerning eligibility, host institutions, application submission, and references, prospective applicants should review the official program materials rather than relying solely on summaries.

International Eligibility

One notable feature of the NASA Hubble Fellowship Program is its international eligibility.

The fellowship is open to English-speaking citizens of all nations.

This means that the program is not limited to U.S. citizens.

Applicants from different countries can therefore apply, provided they satisfy the academic and doctoral-degree eligibility requirements and meet the other requirements specified in the official Announcement of Opportunity.

The fellowship itself is tenable at a U.S. host institution.

Equal Opportunity Statement

National origin

Why the NHFP Can Be Significant for Early-Career Researchers

A postdoctoral fellowship can provide an important transition between doctoral research and a longer-term independent research career.

The NHFP specifically emphasizes independent research, making the program relevant to scientists who want to develop their own research direction in astrophysics.

The potential three-year duration can also provide researchers with an extended period to pursue a substantial research program.

In addition, the opportunity to work at a U.S. host institution of the fellow’s choice, subject to NHFP policies, provides flexibility in selecting a research environment that aligns with the fellow’s scientific interests.

TITLE: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs 2026: Apply for a Funded 1–6 Month International Business Exchange

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Aspiring entrepreneurs and newly established business owners can now apply for the Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs programme, a European business exchange initiative that enables participants to learn directly from experienced entrepreneurs in another participating country.

Unlike a traditional classroom course, employment position or student mobility programme, Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs connects two individual entrepreneurs for a practical period of business collaboration. A new or aspiring entrepreneur spends between one and six months working alongside an experienced host entrepreneur, gaining first-hand knowledge of business development, management, finance, marketing, customer relations and international expansion.

The programme is financed by the European Commission and implemented with the assistance of approved local contact points, including chambers of commerce, start-up centres, incubators and other business-support organisations. Application and participation are free of charge. According to the official programme website, the exchange is partly financed through financial assistance provided to eligible new entrepreneurs.

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs 2026 at a Glance

Programme name: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs

Programme funder: European Commission

Programme management: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency

Exchange duration: One to six months

Exchange format: Entrepreneur-to-entrepreneur business collaboration

Location: Another participating country

Financial support: Monthly country-based financial assistance for eligible new entrepreneurs

Host entrepreneur funding: No European funding is provided to hosts

Application fee: None

Participation fee: None

Application deadline: No deadline; applications are accepted throughout the year

Business sectors: All sectors may be considered

Minimum age: Participants must be over 18

Official application portal: Apply through the Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs IT platform

What Is Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs?

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs is an international business mobility programme created to support people who are planning to establish a business or have recently started one.

The programme helps aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs develop the practical skills required to establish and manage a sustainable small or medium-sized enterprise. Instead of receiving only theoretical instruction, participants work directly with an experienced entrepreneur in another country.

During the exchange, the new entrepreneur observes how an established business operates while contributing their own knowledge, skills, ideas and understanding of their home market. The collaboration is intended to create benefits for both parties.

The new entrepreneur may gain practical business experience, improve a business plan, understand a foreign market and develop international contacts. The host entrepreneur may receive new ideas, specialised knowledge, access to another market and opportunities for future international cooperation.

The exchange can also lead to longer-term commercial relationships, including:

Joint ventures

Contractor and supplier relationships

Cross-border partnerships

Market-entry cooperation

Product development

Business referrals

Subcontracting arrangements

Continued professional collaboration

However, any future relationship must remain separate from the purpose and approval of the original exchange. The programme will not approve arrangements where a pre-existing commercial or personal relationship makes programme support unnecessary.

Who Can Participate as a New Entrepreneur?

Applicants may participate as new entrepreneurs if they fall within one of the following situations:

They are firmly planning to establish their own business and have developed a viable business plan; or

They have already established a business but have less than three years of total entrepreneurial experience.

The business may operate in any sector. There is no restriction requiring applicants to work in technology, manufacturing or another particular industry.

New entrepreneurs must also:

Be over 18 years of age

Be permanently resident in an eligible EU Member State or participating Single Market Programme country

Have a concrete business idea or project supported by a proper business plan

Be motivated to learn from an experienced entrepreneur in another participating country

Be prepared to contribute useful skills, knowledge and competencies to the host business

Be willing to participate actively throughout the agreed exchange

Have sufficient language ability to communicate and collaborate with the proposed host

Be prepared to supplement the programme’s financial assistance if it does not cover every expense

Personally submit the application through the official programme platform

Participate in the programme as a new entrepreneur only once

The programme’s official eligibility requirements are available on the new entrepreneur profile page.

Who Can Participate as a Host Entrepreneur?

Experienced business owners can apply to host an aspiring or newly established entrepreneur.

A host entrepreneur must:

Be permanently resident in a participating country

Have a company registered in that participating country

Be the owner-manager of a micro, small or medium-sized enterprise; or

Be directly involved in entrepreneurship at the board level of an SME rather than serving only as an employee

Have more than three years of experience operating a business as an entrepreneur

Be willing to share business knowledge and experience

Be prepared to mentor the visiting new entrepreneur

Provide a genuine learning and entrepreneurial collaboration

Sign the programme’s Commitment to Quality

Complete an online feedback questionnaire after the exchange

The host must ensure that the visiting entrepreneur receives meaningful business exposure. The programme must not be used to obtain unpaid labour, recruit an intern or fill an ordinary employee position. Full host requirements are explained on the official host entrepreneur profile page.

What Qualifies as a Small or Medium-Sized Enterprise?

Host businesses are generally expected to comply with the European Union definition of a micro, small or medium-sized enterprise.

The main thresholds are:

Micro-enterprise: Fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover or balance-sheet total not exceeding €2 million

Small enterprise: Fewer than 50 employees and annual turnover or balance-sheet total not exceeding €10 million

Medium-sized enterprise: Fewer than 250 employees and annual turnover not exceeding €50 million or a balance-sheet total not exceeding €43 million

The legal form of the business is not necessarily decisive. Independent professionals, self-employed individuals, eligible cooperatives, foundations, associations and certain non-profit organisations may potentially participate if they conduct an economic activity and satisfy the programme’s SME and entrepreneurial requirements.

Participating Countries

Residency requirements differ for new entrepreneurs and host entrepreneurs.

New entrepreneurs must be permanently resident in an EU Member State or a participating Single Market Programme third country.

Eligible EU Member States include:

Austria

Belgium

Bulgaria

Cyprus

Host entrepreneurs may also be based in the following participating non-Single Market Programme destinations:

Canada

United States

Entrepreneurs from EU outermost regions and eligible Overseas Countries and Territories may also participate under the programme’s applicable rules.

Applicants should consult the current official list of participating countries before applying because programme participation and destination availability may change.

How Permanent Residence Is Determined

Eligibility is based primarily on permanent residence rather than nationality.

For an applicant with a registered company, permanent residence is generally treated as the country where that company is registered. Where a company operates through establishments in more than one participating country, the entrepreneur should select the country where they are personally based.

If the applicant does not have a registered company, permanent residence is normally the country where the applicant has spent at least 183 days during the previous 12 months.

An applicant currently living in a non-participating country will normally be considered ineligible, even if that person may satisfy other elements of the residence definition. The detailed residence rules are available in the programme’s permanent residence guidance.

Duration and Structure of the Exchange

An approved Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs exchange can last from one to six months.

The exchange may take place as one continuous stay or may be divided into shorter weekly periods. Where the exchange is divided into separate periods, all approved periods must generally be completed within an overall timeframe of no more than 12 months.

The final duration is agreed between the new entrepreneur and the host entrepreneur and must be approved by their respective local contact points. Acceptance of an initial application does not automatically guarantee a particular host, destination, duration or amount of funding.

The exchange must take place in another participating country. A new entrepreneur cannot complete the exchange in their own country of residence.

What Can Participants Do During the Exchange?

The precise activities are agreed between the new and host entrepreneurs and documented in their activity plan.

Activities may include:

Working alongside and shadowing the experienced host entrepreneur

Studying the host company’s daily management systems

Conducting market research

Identifying new commercial opportunities

Exploring international or cross-border markets

Supporting entrepreneurship-development projects

Participating in innovation and research-related activities

Improving the new entrepreneur’s business plan

Learning about business finance and financial management

Studying customer relationship systems

Understanding pricing and sales strategies

Reviewing branding and marketing practices

Exploring supply chains, operations and business partnerships

Developing new products, services or international business concepts

Learning about the regulatory and cultural environment of another participating country

The exchange should have clear learning objectives for the new entrepreneur and identifiable business value for the host.

Benefits for New Entrepreneurs

New entrepreneurs can gain practical knowledge that may be difficult to obtain through academic study alone.

Potential benefits include:

Up to six months of practical learning with an experienced business owner

Improved understanding of how to establish and manage an SME

Exposure to marketing, sales, accounting, customer relations and business finance

An opportunity to test and strengthen a business plan

Greater confidence in making entrepreneurial decisions

Development of management, technical and sector-specific skills

Better understanding of international and European markets

Experience of different organisational and business cultures

Improved foreign-language and communication skills

Access to a network of international entrepreneurs

Opportunities to identify future business partners

Potential development of cross-border commercial cooperation

Greater awareness of foreign customers, competitors and regulatory conditions

Financial assistance toward eligible travel and living costs

More information is available on the programme’s benefits for new entrepreneurs page.

Benefits for Host Entrepreneurs

Host entrepreneurs do not receive European financial assistance for hosting. However, the programme can provide significant commercial and professional value.

Benefits may include:

Working with a motivated entrepreneur who brings new ideas and perspectives

Accessing skills or specialised knowledge that may not already exist in the host company

Receiving fresh observations about the company’s products, services or processes

Learning about the new entrepreneur’s home market

Identifying opportunities for international expansion

Developing cross-border contacts

Finding potential future business partners

Strengthening the company’s international network

Improving communication and foreign-language skills

Acting as a mentor and contributing to entrepreneurship development

Increasing the company’s international visibility

Exploring future joint ventures, supply relationships or other cooperation

The programme emphasises mutual value: the host provides experience and guidance, while the new entrepreneur contributes ideas, knowledge and practical support. Further details are available on the benefits for host entrepreneurs page.

Financial Support for New Entrepreneurs

Eligible new entrepreneurs may receive financial assistance toward the cost of travelling to and living in the host country.

The assistance:

Is paid by the new entrepreneur’s selected local contact point

Is governed by a financial agreement between the entrepreneur and the local contact point

Is normally calculated according to a monthly lump sum

Depends on the country where the exchange takes place

Covers only the approved period spent abroad collaborating with the host

Is intended to contribute toward travel, accommodation and subsistence expenses

May be paid in several instalments under the signed agreement

May not cover every cost of the exchange

May need to be supplemented with the participant’s own resources

Applicants should treat these figures as contribution rates rather than a promise that all actual costs will be fully covered. The final amount, payment schedule and financial conditions will be established in the agreement with the relevant intermediary organisation. Applicants should verify the latest official monthly financial-assistance table before making travel or accommodation commitments.

Application Documents for New Entrepreneurs

New entrepreneurs should prepare the following before starting their online application:

Curriculum Vitae

The CV should provide a clear and current summary of the applicant’s:

Education

Professional experience

Entrepreneurial experience

Technical competencies

Management capabilities

Business and sector knowledge

The Europass CV format is preferred but is not compulsory. English is strongly encouraged because it can make the applicant’s profile easier for intermediary organisations and potential hosts to understand.

Motivation Statement

The motivation section should explain:

Why the applicant wants to join the programme

What business knowledge they hope to acquire

Why an international exchange is relevant to their business

What skills they can contribute to the host company

How the exchange will strengthen their planned or recently established business

What practical results they expect to achieve

How they will apply the experience after returning home

A generic motivation statement is unlikely to be competitive. It should demonstrate commitment, initiative, seriousness, creativity and clearly defined learning needs.

Full Business Plan

A full business plan is compulsory for new entrepreneurs. A brief idea alone is not sufficient.

The business plan should include at least:

A clear description of the proposed product or service

The problem or customer need addressed

A definition of the target market

Market-size and demand considerations

Competitor analysis

Marketing and sales strategy

Operational requirements

Estimated expenses and revenue for the following two years

Break-even analysis

The applicant’s implementation strategy

The programme does not prescribe a single business-plan template. However, the selected local contact point will assess whether the document is sufficiently complete, viable and professionally prepared.

The full business plan is treated as a confidential document and is generally accessible only to the applicant, the selected intermediary organisation, the programme Support Office and the European Commission.

Business Plan Summary

Applicants must also submit a shorter summary of their business plan. The registration guide indicates a maximum length of 2,000 characters.

Unlike the full confidential business plan, the summary may be visible to accepted entrepreneurs and intermediary organisations in the programme’s online catalogue. Applicants should therefore avoid including trade secrets or other sensitive information.

Language Information

Applicants must be able to communicate effectively with their proposed host. The programme does not provide language training.

There is no universal language examination requirement, but applicants should be comfortable speaking, understanding, reading and writing in the language used during the exchange. The registration guide refers to approximately B2-level ability as a useful benchmark. English is strongly encouraged because it is widely understood across the programme.

Geographical and Sector Preferences

Applicants are asked to identify:

Their principal business sector

Additional sectors relevant to the planned exchange

Their preferred host country

Alternative destination countries

Their proposed exchange duration

The periods during which they are available

Flexibility regarding destinations and dates can increase the likelihood of finding a suitable host.

The complete preparation requirements are explained in the official registration guide for new entrepreneurs.

How to Apply for Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs

The application and matching process generally involves the following stages:

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

Determine whether you qualify as a new entrepreneur or an experienced host entrepreneur. Confirm your permanent-residence status and ensure that your country is currently participating.

Step 2: Identify a Local Contact Point

Select an approved intermediary organisation that operates in your country or region of residence. The organisation will guide you through assessment, matching, preparation and implementation.

Applicants living in an eligible country without an active local contact point may be able to select an intermediary organisation in another participating European country.

Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents

New entrepreneurs should prepare their CV, motivation statement, complete business plan and business-plan summary.

Host entrepreneurs should prepare a detailed professional and company profile, explain their motivation for hosting and identify the skills or experience they can offer.

Step 4: Submit the Online Application Personally

Applications must be submitted through the official programme platform. Participants must not allow an external organisation or third party to submit an application on their behalf.

The official Apply Now page also provides access to explanatory material, registration guides and a preview of the online form.

Step 5: Application Assessment

The selected intermediary organisation reviews the application for eligibility, completeness and quality.

The new entrepreneur registration guide indicates that an initial check should normally be conducted within two weeks of receiving the application. The application may be:

Accepted

Placed on hold pending additional information

Returned to the applicant

Refused

If information is missing, the applicant may be asked to provide it within a specified period. Acceptance gives the participant access to the programme’s online catalogue but does not by itself guarantee an exchange.

Step 6: Find a Suitable Entrepreneur

Accepted participants can pursue a match in two ways:

Suggest an eligible entrepreneur with whom they are already in contact, subject to the programme’s restrictions; or

Search the online catalogue with support from the local contact point.

The proposed host should be relevant to the new entrepreneur’s business objectives and capable of providing genuine entrepreneurial learning.

Step 7: Agree on the Exchange Plan

The two entrepreneurs must agree on:

Exchange dates

Duration

Learning objectives

Proposed activities

Expected contributions from each participant

Anticipated business outcomes

These details must be submitted to the local contact points for assessment and approval.

Step 8: Sign the Required Agreements

All parties digitally sign a Commitment to Quality setting out the objectives and activity plan.

The new entrepreneur also signs a financial agreement with the intermediary organisation. This agreement specifies the funding, responsibilities, payment arrangements, timetable and relevant legal conditions.

Step 9: Complete the Exchange

The new entrepreneur travels to the host country and participates in the agreed activities. Financial assistance is provided according to the signed agreement.

Step 10: Submit Feedback

After the exchange, both entrepreneurs must complete the required feedback questionnaires. The new entrepreneur should explain the activities completed, knowledge acquired and effect of the exchange on their business development.

The complete official process is available on the How to Participate page.

Activities and Relationships That Are Not Permitted

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs is not an internship, employment scheme or source of unpaid labour.

Proposed exchanges may be rejected where:

The host intends to use the new entrepreneur as an ordinary employee or intern

The parties already have a professional relationship that makes programme support unnecessary

The host is already, or plans to become, a co-owner or investor in the new entrepreneur’s business

The new entrepreneur intends to establish a branch of the host’s business

The parties are close relatives, spouses or partners

A significant personal relationship creates a conflict of interest

The new entrepreneur has already worked at the host’s business through another programme

The exchange provides no clear additional value to both businesses

The application is submitted by a third party

Financial assistance is used for a purpose unrelated to the approved exchange

One host entrepreneur cannot host more than one new entrepreneur at the same time. Where co-founders from the same company participate as hosts, their exchanges must take place at different times.

Application Deadline

There is no fixed deadline to register for Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs.

The programme accepts online applications throughout the year, according to its official deadline guidance.

Applicants should nevertheless apply early. The assessment, matching, approval and contracting stages can require considerable time, and the availability and budgets of intermediary organisations may affect when an exchange can begin.

Application Cost

Application and participation are completely free of charge.

No intermediary organisation, consultant or external party should charge an applicant an application or participation fee. Applicants must use the official platform and submit their information personally.

Technical Requirements for Applying

The online application system is designed to work with the latest versions of:

Microsoft Edge

Google Chrome

Mozilla Firefox

Applicants should use a reliable email address that they expect to retain, because the registered email address, first name and last name may not be changeable after registration.

Official Application and Contact Information

Official information page: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs – Apply Now

Online application portal: Start an Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs application

Local contact points: Find an intermediary organisation

Support Office email: support@erasmus-entrepreneurs.eu

Support Office telephone: +32 2 282 08 73

Practical Tips for a Strong Application

Prepare a complete business plan with realistic financial assumptions.

Clearly explain what you need to learn from an experienced entrepreneur.

Describe the specific skills and knowledge you can contribute to the host.

Link every proposed exchange objective to the development of your own business.

Use a professional and updated CV, preferably in English.

Avoid vague statements about wanting international exposure.

Select host countries and business sectors that genuinely match your plans.

Remain flexible about dates and alternative destinations.

Prepare a personal budget because the financial assistance may not cover every expense.

Do not disclose commercially sensitive information in the public business-plan summary.

Apply only through the official programme portal.

Never pay an application or participation fee.

Do not describe the proposed exchange as an internship or employment placement.

Conclusion

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs offers aspiring founders and newly established business owners an opportunity to gain practical international business experience while learning directly from an experienced entrepreneur.

Through a structured exchange lasting between one and six months, new entrepreneurs can strengthen their business plans, develop management skills, explore international markets and establish valuable professional relationships. Experienced host entrepreneurs can benefit from fresh ideas, specialised knowledge and access to potential markets and partners abroad.

The programme is free to join, accepts applications throughout the year and provides eligible new entrepreneurs with country-based financial assistance toward travel and living expenses. Applicants should carefully confirm their residency eligibility, prepare a serious business plan and submit a clear application demonstrating both what they expect to learn and what they can contribute.
